questions.question: Padma Shri awardee Shovana Narayan is associated with which Indian classical dance form?
questions.solution:
Shovana Narayan is a world-renowned Kathak dancer and a disciple of Birju Maharaj.
  • Honor: She was awarded the Padma Shri in 1992 and the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award.
  • Unique Path: She also served as a senior officer in the Indian Audit and Accounts Service, balancing a dual career as a bureaucrat and an artist.

questions.question: Which of the following classical dances is known to be ekaharya, where one dancer takes on many roles in a single performance?
questions.solution:
Bharatanatyam is characterized as Ekaharya, a solo performance style where one dancer plays multiple characters.
  • Narrative: The dancer uses different gestures and positions to shift between roles, such as Krishna, Radha, or a gopi, in a single sequence.
  • Focus: This places immense importance on Abhinaya (facial expressions) and Mudra (hand gestures).

questions.question: Which classical dance form originated in Kuchelapuram village of Krishna district?
questions.solution:
Kuchipudi originated in the village of Kuchelapuram in the Krishna district of Andhra Pradesh.
  • Tradition: It began as a male-dominated dance drama (Bhagavata Mela) performed by Brahmin boys.
  • Pioneer: The legendary Siddhendra Yogi is credited with formalizing the modern structure of this dance form.

questions.question: Which of the following classical dances uses the ‘pung’ as the most important instrument?
questions.solution:
In Manipuri classical dance, the Pung (a drum) is the soul of the performance.
  • Visual: The Pung Cholom is a spectacular part of the repertoire where dancers play the drum while performing athletic leaps and turns.
  • Music: The sound of the Pung provides the primary rhythmic foundation for the lyrical movements of the dance.

questions.question: 'Roppi’ is a popular folk dance from the state of _______________________.
questions.solution:
Roppi is a traditional folk dance from the state of Arunachal Pradesh.
  • Culture: It is performed by local tribes to mark festive occasions and community gatherings.
  • Nature: Like many dances of the Northeast, it is deeply connected to nature and the agricultural cycle.

questions.question: Which state government started the 'Shantala Natya Sri Award' in 1995 in the field of classical dance?
questions.solution:
The Shantala Natya Sri Award was instituted by the Karnataka government in 1995.
  • Inspiration: The award is named after Queen Shantala Devi, the Hoysala queen who was a legendary patron and practitioner of dance (Bharatanatyam and Mohiniyattam).
  • Purpose: It recognizes lifelong achievement and excellence in the field of classical dance.

questions.question: Which of the following is a popular dance form of Punjab?
questions.solution:
Bhangra is the most iconic and energetic folk dance of Punjab.
  • Occasion: Traditionally, it was performed by farmers to celebrate the Vaisakhi festival and the success of the harvest season.
  • Energy: It is characterized by high-energy jumps, shoulder movements, and the loud beat of the Dhol.

questions.question: Shovana Narayan, a Padma Shri recipient, performs which of the following Indian classical dances?
questions.solution:
Shovana Narayan (repeating for emphasis) is an exponent of Kathak.
  • Innovation: She is known for her collaborations with global dancers, bringing Kathak to an international stage while maintaining its classical purity.

questions.question: In which of the following states did the Indian classical dance Bharatanatyam originate?
questions.solution:
Bharatanatyam is the oldest classical dance form of India and originated in Tamil Nadu.
  • Origin: It was formerly known as Sadir and was performed by Devadasis (temple dancers) in the temples of South India.
  • Foundation: It derives its name from Bha (Bhava), Ra (Raga), and Ta (Tala).

questions.question: Which dance of Eastern India was recognized in the Representative List of Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2010?
questions.solution:
Chhau dance, common in Odisha, West Bengal, and Jharkhand, was recognized by UNESCO in 2010.
  • Style: It is a unique blend of martial arts, folk traditions, and storytelling.
  • Types: The three main styles are Seraikella, Mayurbhanj, and Purulia Chhau.

questions.question: With which Indian dance form was Guru Chemancheri Kunhiraman Nair associated?
questions.solution:
Guru Chemancheri Kunhiraman Nair was a legendary master of Kathakali.
  • Longevity: He spent over 80 years promoting and performing the art form and lived to be 104 years old.
  • Honor: He was awarded the Padma Shri in 2017 for his contribution to the classical arts of Kerala.

questions.question: Which dance style was recognised by the famous 'Tanjore Quartet' of the nineteenth century?
questions.solution:
The Tanjore Quartet (four brothers: Ponnayya, Vadivelu, Sivanandam, and Chinnayya) codified the modern format of Bharatanatyam.
  • Impact: They defined the Margam (the standard sequence of items) which includes Alarippu, Jatiswaram, Varnam, Padam, and Tillana.

questions.question: Which of the following classical dance forms from southern India derives its textual sanction from 'Balarama Bharatam' and 'Hastalakshana Deepika'?
questions.solution:
Kathakali derives its technical and textual authority from 'Balarama Bharatam' (written by Karthika Thirunal Bala Rama Varma) and 'Hastalakshana Deepika'.
  • Usage: These texts provide the grammar for the complex mudras and facial expressions used in the dance drama.

questions.question: In which of the following dance forms are four aspects of abhinaya 'angika', 'aharya', 'vachika', 'satvika' and the 'nritta', 'nritya' and 'natya' combined perfectly?
questions.solution:
Kathakali is the form where the five aspects of performance—Angika (body), Aharya (costume/makeup), Vachika (song/speech), Satvika (emotion), and the combination of Nritta/Nritya/Natya—reach a pinnacle of complexity.
  • Visuals: Dancers use elaborate makeup (Vesham) to represent different character types like Pacha (noble) and Kathi (villainous).

questions.question: With which of the following dance forms is Rukmini Devi Arundale associated?
questions.solution:
Rukmini Devi Arundale was the pioneer who spearheaded the revival of Bharatanatyam.
  • Contribution: She moved the dance from temples to the global stage and founded the Kalakshetra academy in Chennai.
  • Distinction: She was the first woman in Indian history to be nominated as a member of the Rajya Sabha.

questions.question: The Popir dance is performed by the Galo tribe of which of the following states?
questions.solution:
The Popir dance is a popular folk dance performed by the Galo tribe in Arunachal Pradesh.
  • Occasion: It is the centerpiece of the Mopin festival, celebrated to seek blessings for a good harvest and to drive away evil spirits.

questions.question: Mayurbhanj Chhau is a tribal dance form of _____.
questions.solution:
Mayurbhanj Chhau is the specific style of Chhau from Odisha.
  • Distinction: Unlike the Purulia and Seraikella styles, Mayurbhanj Chhau is performed without masks, relying purely on body movement and facial expression.

questions.question: ‘Ladaladi’ is a folk dance of the ____________________, in which the bride and bridegroom are lifted upon the shoulders and others dance around the couple.
questions.solution:
Ladaladi is a folk dance of the Bhils (one of India's largest tribal groups).
  • Custom: This dance is a celebratory ritual performed during weddings, where the couple is lifted on shoulders while the community dances in joy.

questions.question: Yamini Krishnamurthy was recognised as the 'Asthana Narthaki' of which style of dance?
questions.solution:
Yamini Krishnamurthy was a dual-specialist and recognized as the Asthana Narthaki (Resident Dancer) of the Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanam for Bharatanatyam and Kuchipudi.
  • Legacy: She played a vital role in popularizing Kuchipudi outside of Andhra Pradesh in the mid-20th century.

questions.question: In the meeting of the Executive Board of Sangeet Natak Akademi held in 2011, it was decided to give how many Akademi Awards in the field of dance?
questions.solution:
In 2011, the Sangeet Natak Akademi decided to increase the number of annual awards in the field of dance to 9.
  • Scope: This ensured representation for all 8 classical dances plus folk/tribal dance forms.

questions.question: Who among the following is NOT associated with Kathakali, a classical dance form of India?
questions.solution:
Kelucharan Mohapatra is the legendary guru associated with Odissi, not Kathakali.
  • Other Options: Ramankutty Nair, Kalamandalam Gopi, and Kalamandalam Rajan are all pillars of the Kathakali tradition.

questions.question: Thanjavur Quartet is best remembered for the revival and codification of which ancient classical dance form?
questions.solution: The Thanjavur Quartet (Tanjore Quartet) are the architects of modern Bharatanatyam. (Repeating to emphasize their historical role in transition from temple to court).

questions.question: Identify the classical dance form that is the principal dance of Northern India.
questions.solution:
Kathak is the principal classical dance form of Northern India.
  • History: It evolved from the itinerant storytellers (Kathakars) of ancient UP and Rajasthan and was later influenced by Persian culture in Mughal courts.

questions.question: Which of the following Vedas mentions dance (Nrti) and danseuse (Nrtu)?
questions.solution:
The Rigveda, the oldest of the four Vedas, contains the earliest mentions of Nrti (dance) and Nrtu (danseuse).
  • Context: It describes dance as a form of divine ritual and artistic expression even in the early Vedic period.

questions.question: Ishira and Maulik Shah jointly received the Sangeet Natak Akademi for the year 2018 for best performance in which dance genre?
questions.solution:
Ishira and Maulik Shah are a famous duo honored by the Sangeet Natak Akademi for their contribution to Kathak.
  • Innovation: They are known for their contemporary approach to Kathak while keeping the traditional Abhinaya and footwork intact.
